absent: Address bias and area bit layout plus region and area structure definitions and table sizes and lock identity beyond observed use.
XZ decoder context layout and progress and error code semantics plus checksum and filter details.
ZSTD context and frame header layout and workspace bound calculations plus maximum window log value.
LZO safe decompression contract and worst case size bound calculation.
Exact fill and flush callback return conventions for partial progress and error propagation.
Device resource tracking and memory region claim primitives plus error pointer encoding.
Resource flag meanings and device tree address translation rules.
Initialization and linkage macros for preboot and static scope plus node and name helpers.

findings.text: The LZO decompression service accepts either a memory pointer or a fill callback for input and either a memory pointer or a flush callback for output, rejects contradictory or missing combinations through an error callback, allocates internal buffers when pointers are absent, optionally tracks consumed input length, and reports success with zero and any failure with negative one.

Header validation requires at least a minimal length, checks a nine byte magic prefix in order, reads a big endian version, skips version dependent library and time fields, interprets a flag bit to decide whether extra filter information is present, then skips mode and time and a variable length name plus trailing checksum, returning success and the total consumed length or failure without side effects.

After the header, decoding proceeds as a loop over blocks where each iteration reads a big endian expected output length with zero meaning end of stream, validates it against the maximum block size, then reads a big endian compressed length plus skipped checksum information, validates the compressed length is positive and not larger than expected, obtains that many input bytes possibly through repeated fills, copies directly when lengths are equal or otherwise safely decompresses and verifies the produced length, then emits through flush or advances the output pointer and compacts any unused streamed input before continuing.
Maximum LZO block size is 262144 bytes, used both to size the internally allocated output buffer when no output pointer is given and as an upper bound that rejects larger declared block lengths.
Header flag value indicating presence of filter information is 2048, tested against big endian flags to decide whether to skip eight bytes or four bytes after version handling.

Minimum possible header length is 33 bytes and maximum possible header length is 297 bytes, respectively used as the entry length guard for parsing and as the initial fill size plus offset that enables copying rather than moving leftover streamed data.
LZO container magic is nine bytes long with decimal values 137 76 90 79 0 13 10 26 10 in order, checked byte by byte at the start of header parsing with any mismatch causing immediate failure.

The generic LZO wrapper forwards its buffer and length and fill and flush and output and position and error arguments directly to the LZO core routine and returns its status unchanged while ignoring its own output length argument.

LZO decoding treats truncated input, oversized declared output, empty or oversized compressed length, allocation failure, decompression failure or length mismatch, and short flush as fatal errors that report through the error callback and return failure after releasing only internally allocated buffers.

The XZ decompression service accepts an input pointer or fill callback and an output pointer or flush callback, initializes checksums when enabled, zeroes the consumed input counter when provided, chooses single call decoder initialization when both callbacks are absent and dynamic allocation otherwise, prepares output and input buffers allocating when needed, and returns zero on stream end else negative one after reporting.

When streaming, XZ decoding loops while the decoder reports progress, refilling exhausted input through fill with accounting, running the decoder, and emptying produced output through flush when full or when decoding finished with pending bytes, then frees any internally allocated input and output buffers and adds final input position to the total.

XZ result mapping treats stream end as success and otherwise reports distinct conditions for out of memory, bad magic, unsupported encoding options, corrupt data or buffer problems, and unexpected internal failure, with allocation failures during setup also reported as out of memory.

The generic XZ wrapper forwards all its input and size and fill and flush and output and usage and error arguments to the XZ core routine unchanged and returns its status, ignoring its own output size argument for sizing decisions.

A bytewise equality helper compares two memory areas for a given length returning affirmative only when all bytes match, and a zeroing helper writes zero bytes across a given length using forward iteration.
XZ streaming input and output buffer size is 4096 bytes, used for allocations when fill or flush callbacks are involved and as the refill chunk size.
Preboot build marker and internal checksum marker are defined to select preboot behavior and built in checksum handling for the XZ decoder.
Architecture specific XZ filter decoders are enabled for x86 and PowerPC and ARM Thumb and ARM and ARM64 and RISC V and SPARC selections.
Preboot memory shims map virtual allocation to plain allocation and map virtual free to plain free guarded against null pointers with statement like safety.

The ZSTD service offers a single chunk path and a streaming path, where the top level without output length treats output as unbounded up to address space limits and delegates to a common worker that chooses the fast single chunk decoder when neither fill nor flush is present and otherwise performs streamed decoding with explicit buffers.

Single chunk ZSTD decoding allocates a workspace sized by a bound query, initializes a decompression context, trims input length to the actual frame size discovered by a size query to ignore trailing junk, decompresses into the supplied output, records consumed input when requested, and always releases the workspace.

Streaming ZSTD decoding ensures an input buffer exists allocating when needed, reads an initial chunk when fill is present, prepares an output buffer allocating when flush is present, decodes the frame header requiring completeness and rejecting oversized windows, allocates a stream workspace sized by the actual window, then loops refilling exhausted input with accounting and running stream decompression until completion while flushing produced bytes and failing on truncation flush shortfall or decode errors, finally accounting remaining input and releasing all internal allocations.

ZSTD error translation returns success when the status code indicates no error and otherwise maps allocation failure and unknown magic and small destination and corruption and checksum problems to distinct human reporting categories with a generic corruption fallback, returning failure in all error cases.
ZSTD streaming chunk size is 131072 bytes, used for input and output allocations and refill sizes when streaming with callbacks.
Maximum allowed ZSTD window size is one shifted left by the maximum window log amount, enforced as an upper bound on the decoded frame header window, and a preboot marker selects preboot behavior.

ZSTD decoding treats input truncation and incomplete header and oversized window and allocation failure and stream decode failure and flush shortfall as fatal errors reported through the error callback with negative return and cleanup of all internal buffers.
Physical frame allowance denies frames marked exclusive, allows frames that are not ordinary RAM, and denies ordinary RAM frames, thereby permitting only non RAM non exclusive regions.
Managed mapping flavor enumeration defines four ordered values starting at zero for default and uncached and write combining and non posted semantics in that order.
Managed mapping release unmaps the stored mapping pointer held in the tracking record.
Managed mapping lookup matches a tracking record when its stored pointer equals the searched address.

Internal managed mapping allocates a pointer sized tracking record on the device node, selects one of four mapping primitives according to the requested flavor, and on success stores the address and registers the record or on failure or allocation miss releases the record and returns null.
Public managed mapping helpers expose default and uncached and write combining flavors by delegating to the internal worker with the corresponding flavor.
Managed unmapping releases the tracking record whose stored address equals the given mapping and warns when no such record exists.

Resource based managed mapping requires a valid device and a memory type resource, upgrades default flavor to non posted when the resource requests it, builds a display name from device and resource names, requests the physical region exclusively, maps it, and on any failure returns an encoded error pointer after releasing any acquired region.

Device tree based mapping converts a node plus index into a resource, optionally reports its length, and delegates to resource based managed mapping, returning an encoded invalid argument error when address translation fails.

Resource mapping failure modes include invalid or non memory resources and name allocation failure and busy region conflict and mapping allocation failure, each encoded as a distinct negative error with prior region claims undone when mapping fails.

Logical mapping searches registered regions under lock for one fully containing the requested range, then claims the first free area slot and invokes the owning region map operation to obtain operations and private data and an offset, encoding the result as a biased address combining slot index and offset, falling back to a warning null returning primitive when no region matches or no slot or map succeeds.

Logical unmapping resolves the address to a live area, forwards to a warning fallback when none exists, otherwise invokes the area specific unmap operation when present and then clears the stored operations and private data under lock.

A single lock serializes region list traversal and area slot allocation during mapping and serializes clearing of area operations and private data during unmapping, ensuring that lookup and allocation and teardown do not interleave.

Area resolution checks that the address carries the expected bias bits warning on mismatch, derives a slot index from dedicated address bits, and returns the slot only when it currently holds operations, otherwise returning null.
Fallback mapping primitives warn about invalid use, with the map fallback returning null and the unmap fallback returning without action.

Logical mapping hazards include requests outside all registered regions and exhaustion of area slots and negative map offsets and missing operations after a seemingly successful map, all of which lead to fallback handling rather than a valid biased address.
